english.title: Dog causing injury in a private place
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the owner]_
(B)_[in charge]_

of a dog, allowed it to enter a place which was not a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY PLACE AND LOCATION..), where it was not permitted to be and, whilst it was there it injured **(..SPECIFY PERSON(S)..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3(3) and (4) of the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991.

english.notes:
(i) 'Private place' is not defined but 'public place' means any street, road or other place (whether or not enclosed) to which the public have or are permitted to have access whether for payment or otherwise, including the common parts of a building containing two or more dwellings. A postman (and other similar visitors to a house) has a licence from the householder to go up a garden path to the door for the purpose of delivering letters. The garden path to a private dwelling is not (normally) a public place.
(ii) DEFENCE: in proceedings for this offence against an owner who was not in charge of the dog, it is a defence under section 3(2) to prove that the dog was, at the material time, in the charge of a person whom he reasonably believed to be fit and proper to be in charge of it.
(iii) A court may make a destruction order and disqualify the offender from having custody of a dog ( section 4 as amended by the Dangerous Dogs (Amendment) Act 1997).
(iv) A court may make a contingent destruction order, see section 4A.

This offence is obsolete from 13th May 2014. For offences committed after this date see offence document H11472.
